title: Fermi estimator
summary: Break an everyday question you cannot look up, such as how long a restaurant queue will take, into a short chain of rough factors joined by ×, ÷ and +, each with a low, best and high guess. See the best estimate to about two significant figures (12 × 10 ÷ 4 ≈ 30 min), the exact range those guesses imply (≈ 13–75 min, never called a confidence interval) on a log-scale axis, and which assumption the answer is most sensitive to, with a suggestion of what to estimate better first. Scale, benchmark and reverse sanity checks, simple unit cancellation, a what-if slider, ten editable examples, copy as text or Markdown, and a narrated beamdswitch deck. Works offline, from file:// and in an iframe.
